feed.title: Combined summary - Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?

entry.title: Combined summary - Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
entry.summary: Over the past two years, substantial advancements have been realized in the management and development of the Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs) repository. The editorial team, comprising six members, has demonstrated a high level of engagement with the community by contributing thousands of comments, processing hundreds of pull requests, and facilitating the publication of numerous BIPs. These efforts have led to a revitalized repository characterized by increased submissions and more dynamic interaction among developers. Notable improvements include the adoption of a revised BIP process, updates to documentation, the resolution of issues related to abandoned proposals, and enhancements to automated integration workflows. Despite these gains, the workload distribution has become uneven, often falling on a single individual, highlighting the demanding nature of maintaining such an essential resource. A more streamlined editorial team consisting of three dedicated members is identified as a practical approach for sustaining effective collaboration and accountability. Recognition is extended to all editors, especially Murch, for their commitment and impact on the BIPs repository’s progress and organization. The preference for a smaller, active group is rooted in the need to balance robust stewardship with manageable workloads, ensuring continued quality and responsiveness in proposal review and repository maintenance. Interest in joining the BIPs editorial team remains strong, as exemplified by Jaroslav Dlouhy’s recent offer to contribute and his inquiry regarding the authorization process. Jaroslav’s ongoing commitment, evidenced by his previous expression of interest, reflects the value placed on proactive contributors who are eager to formalize their roles within the project’s organizational framework. The responsibilities of a BIP Editor are extensive and demand a thorough understanding of Bitcoin’s technical architecture, including consensus mechanisms and protocol details. Proficiency in programming languages relevant to Bitcoin, such as C++ and Python, is considered crucial, alongside experience in open-source collaboration, version control systems like Git, and effective written communication. Clear articulation of technical concepts, meticulous attention to detail, and prior involvement in the development or design of Bitcoin protocols are essential qualifications. Community guidelines and expectations, often disseminated through resources such as the [Bitcoin Development Mailing List](https://groups.google.com/g/bitcoin-development), further inform the role’s requirements. Candidates should be willing to engage deeply with both technical and organizational aspects while upholding the standards of the proposal process. Prospective editors are expected to possess a background in Bitcoin project contributions or protocol design and demonstrate strong English language skills. The role typically requires a weekly commitment of five to ten hours, with flexibility for additional time as needed. Core duties involve monitoring open pull requests, prompting authors for reviews, requesting necessary updates, and merging changes when appropriate. For modifications to existing BIPs, primary review responsibility ideally falls to the original proposal owners, while new BIPs require prompt and comprehensive evaluations by the editors. Constructive feedback and technical feasibility assessments are integral to this process. Most activities associated with BIP editing, except for labeling and merging pull requests, are accessible to any community member. Those interested in becoming involved may begin by engaging with current open pull requests found at [this link](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Apr+-label%3A%22Metadata+Update%22+-label%3ATypo-to-be-collected+-label%3ACI), providing valuable commentary and suggestions. Participation in the BIPs repository extends beyond the official editors, welcoming contributions from all interested parties. Reviewing and offering substantive feedback on open pull requests is encouraged and serves as a meaningful avenue for engagement. Consistent and thoughtful participation not only advances the repository but also enhances a contributor's prospects for future editorial roles. The pace of development can be gradual; nonetheless, sustained involvement and constructive input remain critical in building trust and support within the community. The current editorial workload is increasingly unsustainable, with a backlog of high-quality submissions awaiting review due to limited availability of team members. This persistent challenge underscores the necessity of expanding or refreshing the team. Flexibility in term length is advised, with suggested commitments of 12 to 24 months rather than indefinite service, making editorial positions more accessible to qualified candidates who may be deterred by long-term obligations. Recent correspondence highlights several individuals volunteering or being nominated for editorial roles. Edil, a professor of computer engineering and Head of Research at Vinteum, brings significant experience in peer review and technical specification analysis, notably contributing to projects such as output descriptors, Miniscript ([Vinteum deep dive](https://www.vinteum.org/blog/inside-a-vinteum-deep-dive-the-standards-behind-bitcoin-wallets)), and Stratum V2 ([Vinteum Mining Deep Dive](https://www.vinteum.org/blog/inside-a-vinteum-deep-dive-bitcoin-mining-from-protocol-to-silicon)). His academic background and dedication to detail have been widely acknowledged. Daniela Brozzoni, author of BIP 394 and contributor to BIP 360, offers expertise in blockchain research and active involvement in Bitcoin Core
